summary: Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying at Waseda and Tokyo universities under Kōsen Imakita, Soyen Shaku, and Paul Carus. He held posts at Tokyo, Gakushuin, Columbia, and Otani University (professor 1921–1960).

Daishun Ueyama specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology, studying under Akira Fujieda. He spent his career at Ryukoku University as associate professor (~1970–1977), professor (~1977–2004), and president (~1999–2003).

Daisy Cheung specializes in Indology and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Hong Kong and the University of Hamburg (PhD 2012–2021), later holding posts at Hong Kong and the Austrian Academy of Sciences (postdoctoral fellow 2024).

Daito Shimaji worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku and Otani universities, later teaching at Toyo University (~1914–1927), Komazawa University (~1920–1927), Rissho University (~1924–1927), and the University of Tokyo (1923).

Dale S. Wright worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies, studying under Alan Anderson, Wang Pachow, and Robert P. Scharlemann. He served as professor of religious studies and Asian studies at Occidental College (~1980–2017).

Dalpat Rajpurohit specializes in Indology. He studied at Jai Narain Vyas University, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and Presidency University (PhD 2014–2019), and held posts at Columbia University (lecturer 2008–2018) and the University of Texas at Austin (assistant professor 2019).

Dalsukh Malvania was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar. He held appointments at Banaras Hindu University (~1948–1958), the L.D. Institute of Indology (director ~1958–1977), Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda, and the University of Toronto (~1974–1975).
Damaru Chandra Bhatta is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He earned a PhD from Tribhuvan University and served as associate professor at Tri-Chandra Multiple Campus in 1994.
Damchö Gyatso studied under Penor Rinpoche, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche.
Damdin Badaraev was active in Tibetology and linguistics, studying under Bidia Dandaron and George de Roerich.

Damien Keown specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Lancaster University and the University of Oxford (D.Phil. ~1980–1986), and held academic appointments at Goldsmiths, University of London (~1986–2012; emeritus professor 1995).

Damodar Dharmananda Kosambi worked in Indology and history/archaeology, studying at Harvard under George David Birkhoff. He held posts at Banaras Hindu University, Aligarh Muslim University, Fergusson College, and the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (professor 1945–1962).

Dan Arnold works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Carleton College, Columbia, Iliff, and the University of Chicago (PhD ~1997–2003), and held posts at McGill University and the University of Chicago (2004–2011).
Dan Li specializes in linguistics and Buddhist studies. Li studied under Sherab Gyatso and held a post as associate professor at Soka University (attested 2026).

Dan Lusthaus specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Temple University and held positions at Grinnell College, Bates College, Florida State University, the University of Georgia, and Harvard University (2005).

Dan Martin specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ohio State and Indiana University Bloomington (PhD ~1984–1991), and held posts at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1995–2002) and Swarthmore College (2007).

Dan Smyer Yü works in religious studies and Tibetology. He earned a PhD from the University of California, Davis, and served as research group leader at the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity.

Dan Zahavi is a philosophy scholar who earned a PhD at KU Leuven under Rudolf Bernet and a Dr.phil. at the University of Copenhagen. He has held professorships at Copenhagen (from 2002) and the University of Oxford (2018–2021).

Daniel Aaron Getz works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein, also studying under Ying-shih Yü and Tairyo Makita, and became associate professor at Bradley University (attested 2019).
Daniel Amadé Scheidegger is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed a doctoral degree at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Paul Williams.
